title: Structured vet handoff
why_this_matters: A dog moving from a handler or medic to a veterinarian needs the same structured handoff a person gets; no veterinary handoff study was retrieved, and human evidence for SBAR is only moderate [1].

what_changes_from_human.point: Canine handoffs must carry facts a human handoff does not: breed, measured or estimated weight, DEA 1 blood type if known, MDR1 status and the regular veterinarian, all of which change what the receiving vet can safely give.
A systematic review of SBAR in human care found moderate evidence for improved patient safety, especially for telephone communication, but a lack of high-quality research (human data) [1].

recognition: The app's handoff builder uses the SBAR order: Situation, Background (dog profile), Timeline and interventions, Assessment, Recommendation. This is a design choice, supported only by human data [1].
Weight is marked ESTIMATED when it was not measured; blank fields print as not recorded rather than being guessed.

management: Give the receiving veterinarian: what happened and when, every intervention and time, every drug given (including any human-labelled drug), weight and whether estimated, MDR1 and DEA 1 status, and the dog's regular veterinarian.

takeaway: Hand the receiving veterinarian what happened, what was done and when, and the dog's weight and MDR1 status; say clearly what is estimated or unknown.

sources.citation: Müller M et al. 2018. Impact of the communication and patient hand-off tool SBAR on patient safety: a systematic review (human data). BMJ Open.
